title: The strict /^-?\d+$/ guard exists specifically to defeat the lenient-parseInt t…
body: The strict /^-?\d+$/ guard exists specifically to defeat the lenient-parseInt trap (Number.parseInt('12abc') === 12), but no unit test drives that case: test/tmux-display-message.test.ts covers the empty-field variant ('12;;80;24') instead. I verified the behavior manually against the real helper (non-integer field -> null, see scripts/cam/review-artifact.txt section 3d) so this is a coverage gap, not a defect. Adding a '12abc;5;80;24' case would pin the guard that the doc comment calls load-bearing.

title: Carried from review round 2, still open: MIN_PAYLOAD_TAIL_MATCH = 2 is a loose …
body: Carried from review round 2, still open: MIN_PAYLOAD_TAIL_MATCH = 2 is a loose anchor, and a false positive costs a duplicate push (the back-to-back send-keys race). The 2-char floor is only needed for the exact residue where the composer's trailing row holds precisely the prompt-width remnant. Deriving the expected remnant length from the already-sampled paneWidth and cursorX would make the check exact rather than probabilistic over a scanned suffix range.

title: src/tmux/dispatch.ts was raised 365 -> 583 (+60%) across this branch, with a we…
body: src/tmux/dispatch.ts was raised 365 -> 583 (+60%) across this branch, with a well-argued per-file _ref staged in the same commit, so the raise is justified rather than papering over a split. Noting for the next story that touches this file: dispatch.ts now carries three distinct concerns (idle detection, the geometry delivery oracle plus its content backstop, and the logEvent adapters at :545-582). If it grows again, the logEvent adapter pair (adaptLogEventForPush + makePushLogEvent) is the natural extraction.

Pre-existing drift the diff correctly did not touch under surgical-changes discipline.

body: One em-dash was added in the US-003 patterns.md bullet, against the global convention of no em-dash in persisted human-readable .md. Non-blocking: the file already carries 23 em-dashes on main, so the added line follows established local style, and no automated gate checks this.
